standard.title: Share and display artworks in informal settings
standard.description: share and/or display artworks and/or visual arts practice in informal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can share artworks in informal settings, choosing audience and format and explaining their work (AC9AVA2P01). They have basic experience of multiple sharing contexts. They have not yet selected documentation of a process to share, curated a display, or produced an artist statement.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share and/or display artworks and visual arts practice in informal settings, selecting documentation and making decisions about appropriate audiences and presentation formats.

nodes.label: Selecting and arranging for display
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select examples from their visual arts practice and arrange them to communicate the development of their ideas.
nodes.minimum_width: Select at least two examples from their practice (experiments, in-progress work, final artwork) and arrange them to show how ideas developed.
nodes.typical_width: Select a range of documentation (experiments, compositional approaches, reflections, final artwork) and arrange in a visual display; explain the sequence and what it shows about the development of ideas.
wider: Trial two different arrangements of the same artworks — compare which communicates the development of ideas more clearly and explain why
Arrange a physical wall display and then consider what would need to change to share the same works on a digital platform

response_modes.reason: Curation — selecting and arranging to communicate — is a new skill at this level. Students need to understand that arrangement communicates meaning, not just that display looks tidy. Structured questions ('What does this arrangement say about how your ideas grew?') support the curatorial reasoning.

success_criteria: Selects at least two examples from their practice to form a display
Arranges them in a way that shows development — can explain what the arrangement communicates

nodes.label: Producing an artist statement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce a written or spoken artist statement that explains the ideas, themes and meanings in their artwork.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a spoken or written artist statement that explains one idea or meaning in their artwork.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss and document ideas, themes and meanings; produce written or spoken artist statements; explore multimedia formats for combining artwork with statement.
wider: Create a multimedia artist statement — combine photographs of the making process with spoken explanation of ideas and decisions
Identify and explain your own and another artist's choices in art-making — use the comparison to sharpen your explanation of your own choices

response_modes.reason: Artist statements require repeated practice to develop from superficial description ('I painted a sunset') to genuine explanation of intent ('I used orange and red to communicate the feeling of heat fading'). Consolidation across multiple artworks builds depth.

success_criteria: Produces a spoken or written artist statement
The statement explains an idea, theme or meaning — not only what the artwork shows

nodes.label: Choosing audience and format
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make deliberate decisions about appropriate audiences for their work and choose presentation formats suited to each context.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify an appropriate audience for one artwork and explain why that audience is suitable.
nodes.typical_width: Choose appropriate audiences and formats across multiple sharing contexts — folio, peer circle, digital platform, physical display, school community exhibition; explain how format choices serve the audience and purpose.
wider: Plan a class exhibition for a specific audience (younger students, families, community) — make decisions about layout, labels, accessibility and purpose
Adapt an existing physical display for a digital sharing context — consider what changes and what can be preserved

response_modes.reason: Students bring together their curatorial skills, artist statement capability and audience awareness to make a complete sharing decision — who, how and in what context the work is best shared.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Exhibition planning for different audiences (younger students, community, digital) each requires different decisions — students who plan for multiple audience types build versatile presentational thinking.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one appropriate audience for a sharing context and gives a reason
Makes at least one format choice (display, digital, folio, verbal) suited to that audience
